## How to use this site

Each lesson combines a business question, an executable example, an explanation of what each transformation changes, and practice tasks. Run the code yourself: change one input, predict the result, and then inspect the output. That cycle is more valuable than copying a finished pipeline.

::: {.callout-tip title="A reliable analysis habit"}
Before writing code, state the **unit of observation** (for example, one row per order) and the **decision metric** (for example, net revenue by region). After every join or pivot, check row counts, key uniqueness, and missing values. These checks prevent technically valid code from producing misleading conclusions.
:::

## Learning route

1. Begin with [R setup and projects](modules/module-1/installing-r.qmd).
2. Build core programming skills in [R fundamentals](modules/module-2/index.qmd).
3. Learn tidyverse workflows in [Module 3](modules/module-3/index.qmd) and data types in [Module 4](modules/module-4/index.qmd).
4. Apply `dplyr` to business data in [Module 5](modules/module-5/index.qmd).
5. Reshape and validate tabular data in [Module 6](modules/module-6/index.qmd).

Need help? Read the [support guide](course/support.qmd) and include a minimal reproducible example when asking a coding question.
